_comment: Annotated example for poll_connector.py --config, targeting Splunk's own REST Search API in 'oneshot' mode -- a single blocking request that runs an SPL search synchronously and returns real single-JSON results, unlike the usual async create-job-then-poll search flow (which needs multiple requests PollerConfig can't do). Point base_url at YOUR Splunk management port (default 8089) and adjust the search string to your own notable-event index/fields. Delete this _comment field (or leave it; it's ignored) before using.
name: splunk-es-notable
_comment_auth: Splunk's token-auth feature (Settings > Tokens, Splunk 7.3+) issues a long-lived bearer token -- no OAuth2/session dance needed. auth_token_env names an ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE holding the real token; never put the token itself in this file.
_comment_search: exec_mode=oneshot makes Splunk run this search synchronously and return results in this one response. Adjust the SPL to your own ES notable-event index and field names.

static_query_params.search: search index=notable | fields _time, rule_name, urgency, src, dest, dvc, signature, event_id, mitre_technique_id | sort 0 _time

_comment_records_path: Splunk's oneshot response body is {"results": [...]} -- one flat dict per matched event.
_comment_cursor: earliest_time narrows the SPL search to events after the last one seen. Splunk accepts an epoch or ISO8601 string here -- verify which format your Splunk instance actually renders _time as in JSON output and adjust if incremental polling seems to skip or repeat events.
_comment_normalizer: Uses the real Splunk ES notable-event normalizer (ingestion/normalizers.py:normalize_splunk) instead of a generic field_map -- it understands urgency's five-value scale (including 'informational') and extracts MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs, neither of which a flat field_map alone can do.
